posts.title: Turn buying signals into pipeline with Sendoso gifts in Genie One
posts.summary: Created a Databricks Marketplace MCP server that lets Genie One call Sendoso’s gifting API, turning data signals into automated, governed gift actions.
posts.issue: Teams had to export data and switch tools to send gifts, slowing down outreach.

posts.title: Accelerate GPU training on Unity Catalog tables with UCDataset
posts.summary: Created UCDataset, a native PyTorch loader that streams Unity Catalog tables directly to each GPU, eliminating copies and speeding data delivery.
posts.issue: GPUs spent time idle waiting for data, raising training cost and time.

posts.title: Workflow SDK now writes over WebSockets on Vercel
posts.summary: Switched event and stream writes to a persistent WebSocket, cutting request overhead and delivering token streams 4.2× faster.
posts.issue: Many HTTP requests slowed down streaming AI token output and raised costs.

posts.title: Using AI to Build AI: How Agentforce Engineers Scale Automation Without Sacrificing Reliability
posts.summary: They created an AI‑driven automation pipeline that generates and validates components, using tool calls and safety checks to keep reliability high.
posts.issue: Engineers needed to automate building the Atlas Reasoning Engine without unreliable AI-generated code.

posts.title: Chat SDK agents can now stream generative UI with json-render
posts.summary: Created a JSON‑based UI spec that agents output, which json‑render turns into native cards for Slack, Teams, etc., streaming updates as the spec builds.
posts.issue: Developers had to create separate UI code for each chat platform, slowing down agent responses.

posts.title: AI Gateway adds DeepSeek Search and Fetch tools
posts.summary: Added DeepSeek Search and Fetch tools to AI Gateway, letting any model that supports tool calling retrieve page titles, URLs, summaries, and markdown content via a single API key.
posts.issue: Developers needed a simple way to let LLMs fetch web pages and search results during tool‑calling tasks.

posts.title: Safe and Efficient Multi-Epoch Embedding Training
posts.summary: Created a multi‑epoch training pipeline that pre‑trains ID embeddings with a contrastive objective and then fine‑tunes them safely, avoiding memorization.
posts.issue: Fine‑tuning embeddings for only one epoch limited model quality on fresh data.

posts.title: Speed Up Image Generation with FLUX 3 Image Klein on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
posts.summary: They optimized the FLUX 3 Image Klein model with TensorRT, fused kernels, multi‑GPU parallelism, FP8/NVFP4 quantisation and caching, cutting latency dramatically.
posts.issue: Image generation was too slow for design tools and workflows.

posts.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning Weight Refit with the Reshard Collective
posts.summary: They created a new Reshard collective that moves only needed weight shards directly between training and inference GPUs, cutting redundant data transfer.
posts.issue: Updating model weights on inference GPUs was slow and used too much network bandwidth.

posts.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
posts.summary: Created PDD Kit, a toolkit that lets agents generate formal proofs from natural‑language specs, ensuring the code matches the contract for all inputs.
posts.issue: Agent‑written code often drifts from the original specification, and tests miss many bugs.

posts.title: Analyze your Stripe data directly with your agent
posts.summary: Stripe added APIs that let agents like Claude retrieve and query over 300 structured tables, generate SQL, and return results for natural‑language prompts.
posts.issue: Customers wanted to ask AI agents to analyze their Stripe data without writing code.

posts.title: Reflex: an architecture for building mobile apps with agents
posts.summary: Created Reflex, an MVVM architecture that runs app logic headlessly and exposes state via a CLI, letting agents test iOS and Android with a single test suite.
posts.issue: Testing mobile screens required slow emulator builds, delaying agent-written code verification.

posts.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
posts.summary: Apple trained tiny neural networks offline to learn how typical queries map to the best document vectors, routing queries quickly to the right cluster for faster retrieval.
posts.issue: Searching millions of document vectors was slow and costly, hurting response time for user questions.

posts.title: How two engineer side projects became the agent taking action inside Dropbox
posts.summary: Created a sandboxed agent that connects to Dropbox via rclone, uses permission checks and version history to safely modify files and allow rollbacks.
posts.issue: Users wanted AI to edit their Dropbox files but needed safety and control over changes.

posts.title: How AI-assisted development helped us build the new Dropbox experience
posts.summary: They used AI to generate code, implement features, and run tests, letting engineers review and approve the work, enabling fast cross‑platform delivery.
posts.issue: Engineers needed to add complex new features to web and desktop quickly, but development was slow and fragmented.

posts.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro now has more ZDR providers on AI Gateway
posts.summary: Vercel added more Zero Data Retention providers to its AI Gateway, routing requests only to compliant partners and removing platform fees, so teams can use Kimi models cost‑effectively and securely.
posts.issue: Users wanted a cheaper, privacy‑safe way to use Kimi models without extra fees or data leaks.

posts.title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
posts.summary: Created Vercel Schedules, an API/SDK that lets code create, update, or cancel one‑time and recurring jobs, which are triggered via queues while the app runs.
posts.issue: Developers needed a way for agents and apps to run tasks on dynamic schedules without redeploying or managing separate databases.

posts.title: Scaling Model Evaluation at Pinterest with Ray (Part 4)
posts.summary: They combined Ray with Spark to compute metrics during inference, using accumulators to aggregate results on the fly, cutting evaluation time by up to 32%.
posts.issue: Running many model experiments caused slow, costly evaluation pipelines.

posts.title: Use NVIDIA NeMo to Turn Agent Failures into Tests and Harness Fixes
posts.summary: They built a loop using NeMo Compass to turn trace logs into prioritized test cases, wrote evaluations with NeMo Eval Author, and refined prompts, routing and memory to fix the agent.
posts.issue: Agents sometimes pick the wrong tool or miss context, causing task failures.

posts.title: How NVIDIA Uses AI Agents to Streamline AI Factory Operations
posts.summary: NVIDIA built an AI Factory Operations Agent that uses multiple specialized agents, connected via a protocol, to diagnose issues and suggest fixes through a chat interface.
posts.issue: SREs had to check many dashboards manually to find why training performance dropped.

posts.title: How NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint Coordinates AI Agents to Investigate Production Issues
posts.summary: Created a factory manager AI agent that connects to existing data and tools, monitors operations, finds root causes, and directs robots to fix problems.
posts.issue: Unplanned factory downtime costs millions and investigating issues takes too much time.

posts.title: Honeycomb Team Agents: AI SRE Done Right
posts.summary: Created AI agents that read code, logs, runbooks and tickets, set goals, run continuously, and proactively suggest fixes or actions.
posts.issue: SRE teams spend too much time reacting to alerts instead of preventing problems.

posts.title: How Zapier turns ideas into working software in hours with Vercel
posts.summary: They used Vercel’s v0 platform to spin up interactive, multi‑view demos in under two hours, letting backend engineers deliver clickable experiences without frontend design time.
posts.issue: Teams needed to show partners working prototypes quickly, but the process took weeks.

posts.title: How Mercor ships internal apps and billions of production tokens on one platform
posts.summary: They added Vercel AI Gateway to route requests across providers, adding capacity and failover, reducing batch time to 2‑3 hours.
posts.issue: Batch jobs were stuck for up to 12 hours because model rate limits caused retries.

posts.title: F3 Lightning: How Meta Accelerates Ads ML Features to Production at Scale
posts.summary: Created a DAG compiler that merges feature graphs, sharing common operations so each computation runs only once per request.
posts.issue: Feature extraction duplicated work, causing slow and costly ad model predictions.

posts.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
posts.summary: Created a synthetic data platform that generates realistic enterprise workspaces and runs automated evaluation pipelines to measure AI performance.
posts.issue: Need to test Copilot accuracy without exposing sensitive enterprise data.

posts.title: Vercel MCP now supports MCP events
posts.summary: They created an event system that lets agents subscribe to deployment events via managed webhooks, handling filtering, expiration, and limits automatically.
posts.issue: Developers had to poll Vercel for deployment updates, wasting time and resources.

posts.title: Run AI Models for Edge Application Development with Just a Few Commands
posts.summary: NVIDIA created TensorRT Edge-LLM, a lightweight C++ runtime that builds optimized inference engines on DGX Spark, enabling quick deployment on Jetson and DRIVE platforms with speculative decoding for faster generation.
posts.issue: Developers struggled to run large AI models on embedded devices due to heavy setup and slow inference.

posts.title: Build Specialized Agents on a Stack You Control with NVIDIA NemoClaw
posts.summary: NVIDIA released NemoClaw blueprints that bundle model, harness, and governance tools, letting teams plug into existing harnesses like OpenClaw, Hermes, or LangChain and deploy agents safely and efficiently.
posts.issue: Developers needed a secure, customizable stack to run specialized agents with enterprise data.

posts.title: Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo
posts.summary: NVIDIA created AICR, a validated recipe that bundles Dynamo with all required GPU drivers, scheduling, networking and monitoring, so teams can deploy and test models quickly.
posts.issue: Deploying AI inference on Kubernetes was slow and error‑prone because many components had to be set up manually.

posts.title: Speeding up language models for travel applications
posts.summary: They trained a smaller model using knowledge distillation and added Medusa heads to predict several tokens at once, cutting cost and latency dramatically.
posts.result: Cost under one‑third, up to 20× faster
posts.issue: Large language models were too slow and expensive for travel site queries, hurting user experience and revenue.

posts.title: The fx adapter now runs the harness on the host
posts.summary: Moved the harness to run in the host process with libfx, isolating filesystem tools, adding tool filtering, mid‑turn steering, structured output, and session resume.
posts.issue: Setting up sandboxed tool execution was complex and kept credentials insecure.

posts.title: Catching Bugs Before They Land: JiTTesting’s Human-on-the-Loop Approach at Full Scale
posts.summary: They built a system that uses LLMs to automatically write tests for each code change and an LLM‑as‑judge ensemble to filter out false positives.
posts.issue: Code changes introduced bugs faster than traditional tests could catch, risking production issues.

posts.title: Vercel Agent can now validate alerts before paging
posts.summary: They added an Agent that reviews each monitor alert, checks logs and metrics, and only forwards alerts classified as Critical to the paging webhook.
posts.issue: Too many non‑critical alerts were paging on‑call engineers, causing noise and fatigue.

posts.title: Run Paseo agents on Vercel Sandbox
posts.summary: They added a Vercel Sandbox plugin that runs agents in the cloud, saves files and conversation history, and reuses the AI gateway key across sessions.
posts.issue: Developers wanted to run AI agents continuously and switch devices without losing state.

posts.title: Box Mount now runs in Vercel Sandbox
posts.summary: Created Box Mount that syncs a Box folder to a Vercel Sandbox directory, letting agents use normal file commands while keeping credentials separate.
posts.issue: Agents needed a way to read and write Box files without exposing credentials.

posts.title: Introducing Vercel CI
posts.summary: Built Vercel CI that only runs the tasks affected by a code change, reuses cached results, and gives each task just enough compute, cutting wait time 2‑6×.
posts.issue: CI runs full pipelines for every tiny change, making developers and bots wait too long.

posts.title: Replit’s Architecture Behind Secure Agent Work
posts.summary: Replit added isolation, firewall rules, and policy‑driven controls in its Agent Habitat platform to limit what agents can read or write and to automatically enforce security rules.
posts.issue: Agents could be exploited to cause damage, so companies need secure guardrails and monitoring.

posts.title: Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design
posts.summary: Meta co‑designed a new model, system architecture, and custom GPU hardware to run a much larger neural network with hierarchical indexing and GPU‑native operators, achieving near‑ranking quality at retrieval speed.
posts.result: tens of millions ads/second per GPU
posts.issue: Retrieving relevant ads from billions of candidates was too slow and expensive for high‑quality models.

posts.title: Vercel Agent sessions now cost 67% less
posts.summary: They redesigned context handling and improved prompt‑cache reuse, so each session needs fewer tokens and runs cheaper.
posts.issue: Agent sessions used many tokens, making them expensive for users.

posts.title: Anyone can now bring their ideas into the company codebase
posts.summary: Replit built Cloud Agents that turn plain‑language requests into safe code changes, test them, and handle pull‑request reviews automatically.
posts.issue: Non‑technical team members can't directly modify core code, causing slow review bottlenecks.

posts.title: Beyond the Prompt: Engineering the Loop for Software Change at Scale
posts.summary: Created a Loop system that combines prompts, reusable skills, and sub‑agents to automate iOS component migration, handling failures and decisions autonomously.
posts.result: Two‑year effort finished in three months
posts.issue: Large code changes were slow because hidden dependencies and build failures required constant human intervention.

posts.title: Key Takeaways from Tech at Agoda: From Assistants to AI Agents
posts.summary: Agoda created AI agents that take on planning, code review, support triage and testing, using clear goals and human approval steps to keep work safe.
posts.issue: Engineers wrote code faster, but planning, testing and release became bottlenecks.

posts.title: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Nemotron to Know Local Rules, Not Just Local Languages
posts.summary: NVIDIA fine‑tuned Nemotron with country‑specific persona datasets, adding synthetic local demographics and regulations so the model answers with correct regional information.
posts.issue: The model gave generic, inaccurate answers for local French and Belgian queries, missing regional rules and cultural nuance.

posts.title: 3 Ways to Boost MoE Inference on NVIDIA DGX Spark
posts.summary: They replaced the MoE kernel with a runtime‑compiled version that caches binaries and reduced weight traffic, letting the model generate more tokens per step.
posts.issue: MoE inference was slow because reading model weights limited token generation speed.

posts.title: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI
posts.summary: They added an LLM layer to read logs, extract error details, and suggest fixes, while keeping existing rule‑based logic for known cases.
posts.issue: Half of failed jobs were unclassified, wasting engineer time.

posts.title: Bringing foundational models to the front lines of TB screening
posts.summary: Created and fine‑tuned a foundation model that reads chest X‑rays, runs on low‑resource devices, and flags TB like an expert radiologist.
posts.issue: Remote clinics lack radiologists, causing many TB cases to be missed.

posts.title: Using AI Agents to Teach Robots Like Microduck to Walk in Simulation
posts.summary: Created a workflow where AI agents generate plans, build simulated environments, and train navigation policies using NVIDIA's RTX Spark, Nemotron, and Isaac Lab, then evaluate them in simulation.
posts.issue: Robots struggled to learn walking and obstacle navigation without a coordinated planning and training system.

posts.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
posts.summary: They created Flint‑interactive, a high‑level language that turns user or agent commands into semantic events, letting a compiler generate and update interactive visualizations automatically.
posts.issue: Users wanted charts they could explore, not just static images.

posts.title: The science behind TorchNeuron, Amazon’s new PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium chips
posts.summary: Created TorchNeuron, a backend that translates PyTorch ops to Trainium, adds multi‑level caching and adaptive eager grouping to boost performance.
posts.issue: Developers needed to run PyTorch models on Trainium without rewriting code, while keeping speed and cost low.

posts.title: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment
posts.summary: Created Remote Dev, a cloud‑based Mac environment that gives each AI agent its own sandbox to compile, run simulators, and create PRs, all triggered from Slack.
posts.issue: AI agents were overloading developers' laptops when building and testing mobile apps.

posts.title: Replit Monitoring Agent: Your very own software engineering team
posts.summary: Created an autonomous monitoring agent that watches app health, diagnoses problems from logs, writes and validates a fix, and can deploy it automatically.
posts.issue: Small teams must manually find and fix app outages, which wastes time and frustrates users.

posts.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
posts.summary: They created ThinkingBox, a system that runs agents against a real database, checks the final state, and uses that check as a reward signal to fine‑tune the agent.
posts.issue: Agents often said they finished tasks even when the database still needed work.

posts.title: Running Frontier-Class AI Models Across 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark Nodes
posts.summary: NVIDIA built an eight‑node DGX Spark cluster that links eight servers, giving 1 TB unified memory and faster communication, letting huge models run and be served locally.
posts.issue: Developers need to run very large models and multiple models together, but single machines lack enough memory and speed.

posts.title: How Shopify turns open models into task experts
posts.summary: Created specialized sub‑agents by post‑training open models with a continual learning loop and an LLM judge, then swapped them in for the main model.
posts.issue: Token‑heavy tasks cost too much and run slowly on the main model.

posts.title: Empowering frontline maternal care with AI-assisted ultrasound
posts.summary: They built an AI model that reads blind‑sweep ultrasound scans from cheap portable probes and runs on mobile devices, letting frontline workers assess gestational age.
posts.issue: Many regions lack trained sonographers, leaving pregnant people without ultrasound access.

posts.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
posts.summary: They redesigned the tokenizer to focus on token cost for the specific domain, keeping the same base model and training data.
posts.issue: Using a generic vocabulary made the model write too many tokens, raising inference cost.

posts.title: Inside NVIDIA Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime
posts.summary: They created NVIDIA Sentry, a hardware‑based framework on BlueField‑4 DPUs that watches agent actions, checks requests, and enforces policies outside the agent’s reach.
posts.issue: AI agents could bypass security controls and misuse tools or data.

posts.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale
posts.summary: They created OpenShell, an open‑source runtime that controls what files, services, and devices an agent can access, adds monitoring, and lets operators block or modify actions.
posts.issue: Autonomous agents could perform unsafe actions when working on long, complex tasks.

posts.title: Developing an AI Factory Digital Twin with an Agent-Assisted Workflow
posts.summary: Created an Omniverse DSX Blueprint with reusable assets and scripts, and added AI agents that gather inputs, assemble OpenUSD scenes, and let engineers review and iterate designs.
posts.issue: Developers struggled to combine site plans, equipment data, and engineering specs into a single, editable digital twin model.

posts.title: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search
posts.summary: They created a model that generates protein sequences and structures together, then runs a reward‑guided search at inference time, keeping and expanding promising partial designs until the goal is met.
posts.result: Faster and uses less memory than the previous version
posts.issue: Scientists need to explore billions of protein sequences to find therapeutic candidates, but exhaustive search is impossible.

posts.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
posts.summary: They added an edge script that injects structured tools into pages, letting agents call exact functions like search_products instead of guessing clicks.
posts.issue: Merchants needed a way for AI agents to shop on their sites without breaking when pages change.

posts.title: Cross-store product clustering across millions of stores
posts.summary: They created tiered matching models, graph partitioning, and a learned merge step to cluster billions of listings across stores into a single identifier.
posts.issue: Different merchants list the same product in many ways, making it hard to show a unified view.

posts.title: How We Deploy Reliably at Razorpay
posts.summary: They built a progressive canary system that rolls out changes in tiny steps, uses AI judges to compare logs and metrics, and automatically rolls back if errors appear.
posts.issue: Deployments often introduced bugs that broke payments, hurting merchants and customers.

posts.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
posts.summary: They created a thin orchestrator that only sequences tasks and checks reliability, while 14 specialized agents handle each domain, cutting context overload.
posts.issue: The main AI agent kept hallucinating because it had to handle all domain knowledge and routing.

posts.title: GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary
posts.summary: Created GenRecs Tokenization, turning each ad, product, or page into a short sequence of semantic tokens using LLM embeddings, so the model can reason about unseen items like familiar ones.
posts.issue: Ads struggled to recommend brand‑new products because they had no past click data.

posts.title: From Static Help Content to a RAG-Based Onboarding Agent for Partners
posts.summary: Built a chatbot inside the sign‑up flow that pulls help‑center articles, ranks them, and generates answers grounded in that content.
posts.issue: Partners get stuck in the long, confusing registration flow and need instant help without a human.

posts.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
posts.summary: They traced token usage, improved the reviewer code, switched models, and increased cache hits, cutting review cost by 68% and speeding up reviews.
posts.issue: Inference costs for code reviews kept rising, hurting the budget.

posts.title: Advancing Generative Recommendation Inference: our collaboration with NVIDIA on TensorRT LLM
posts.summary: Spotify built a generative recommendation system that uses a large language model with beam search to generate semantic IDs, then switched from vLLM to NVIDIA TensorRT LLM for GPU‑optimized inference.
posts.issue: Personalized recommendations needed real‑time, multi‑surface inference that could scale beyond a proof‑of‑concept.

posts.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents
posts.summary: They replaced freeform reasoning with a set of reusable reasoning options and let the model pick the best one, scoring all options in parallel.
posts.result: Per‑turn latency dropped 90%, overall inference latency 28–54% faster
posts.issue: Long, costly reasoning slowed multimodal search agents.

posts.title: Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio
posts.summary: They used Apple’s MLX framework and RDMA over Thunderbolt to run trillion‑parameter models on one or multiple Mac Studios, achieving fast token generation.
posts.issue: Running large language models locally was too slow or required expensive cloud resources.

posts.title: Scale Agentic Coding Workflows with Meta’s Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
posts.summary: Created Muse Spark Open, an 816B MoE model with a 1 M‑token window that plans, uses tools, observes results, and self‑corrects across entire projects.
posts.issue: Developers needed an AI that could handle huge codebases and multi-step refactoring without breaking tasks into pieces.

posts.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Powers Specialized Agents with Multimodal Reasoning
posts.summary: NVIDIA created Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B‑parameter MoE model that handles text, image, document, and video inputs, reasons, follows instructions, and calls tools, all on a single GPU.
posts.issue: Enterprise workflows need agents that can read documents, follow policies, and use multiple tools in one request.

posts.title: Squeezing ~2× MFU out of our training runs
posts.summary: They rewrote the attention kernel, integrated it with the compiler, and tuned the optimizer, which doubled the model‑flops‑utilization during training.
posts.issue: Training large Transformer models was slow and under‑utilized the hardware.

posts.title: PathSeer: Adaptive Filtered Vector Search
posts.summary: We added the PathSeer algorithm to the HNSW index, letting the system choose the best order for distance and filter checks, which speeds up filtered searches.
posts.issue: Filtered vector searches were slow and unreliable when filters changed frequently.

posts.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
posts.summary: Created a Geospatial Reasoning agent that plans steps, picks the right Earth AI models, and calls tools like Maps, Earth Engine, and custom datasets to answer spatial questions.
posts.issue: Standard LLMs can’t handle huge, complex geospatial data and multi‑step spatial analysis.

posts.title: Measuring the Impact of Personalized Recommendations
posts.summary: They built a behavioral model that separates a member’s underlying preference from the extra effect of a recommendation, allowing causal measurement of recommendation impact.
posts.issue: How much value does personalized recommendation add to user viewing?

posts.title: Integrating Netflix’s Foundation Model into Personalization applications
posts.summary: Created a single foundation model and integrated it into production using embeddings, subgraph queries, and daily fine‑tuning to serve different latency and stack needs.
posts.issue: Multiple specialized models made personalization hard to maintain and update.

posts.title: Optimizing Agent Reliability and Tool Calling Efficiency for Chip Design Using NVIDIA NeMo Gym
posts.summary: Used NVIDIA NeMo Gym to test and refine the Siemens Fuse EDA agent, adding verifiers and better tool descriptions, which raised benchmark scores to ~95% and cut agent turns by 66%.
posts.issue: AI agents often produce plausible but wrong results, risking errors that spread through chip design workflows.

posts.title: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query
posts.summary: They created CASTLE, a system that synthesises realistic search queries and relevance labels from booking data, then trains a retrieval model on this joint synthetic data.
posts.issue: Airbnb needed natural‑language search but had no real user queries or relevance labels to train on.

posts.title: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
posts.summary: Created a 24B‑parameter MoE model with only 2B active parameters per token, chain‑of‑thought output, large 131K context, and tool‑calling ability, enabling cheap continuous on‑device inference.
posts.result: Leads on five tool‑use benchmarks, three‑times next best on AutomationBench
posts.issue: Need fast, private on‑device agents that can reason and use tools without heavy compute.

posts.title: Inside Razorpay’s RTO Model: The Engineering Behind its ML Lifecycle
posts.summary: They built a risk model that scores each checkout, then a policy decides whether to show COD; outcomes are logged to evaluate and retrain the model.
posts.issue: Showing cash‑on‑delivery could cause costly returns, but hiding it may lose sales.

posts.title: How to Rewrite Apache Spark UDFs for GPU Acceleration with AI Agents
posts.summary: They created AI agents that automatically rewrite UDFs into GPU‑compatible code, letting Spark run fully on GPUs and boosting speed over 20×.
posts.issue: Custom Spark UDFs slowed down queries and prevented GPU acceleration.

posts.title: Can we change an AI model’s architecture without retraining it from scratch?
posts.summary: They introduced priming, which reuses pretrained Transformer weights to quickly convert them into hybrid models, cutting pretraining cost by over 99%.
posts.issue: Training new hybrid model architectures costs huge GPU time and money.

posts.title: Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
posts.summary: Created Minions, a system that gathers idle Apple Silicon GPUs from Macs, schedules inference jobs across them, and handles failures to boost compute capacity.
posts.issue: Teams needed more GPU power for inference but buying new hardware was expensive and slow.

posts.title: Automating Data Ingestion with a RAG Flywheel
posts.summary: Created a RAG flywheel that stores past mappings, uses vector embeddings for semantic search, and an LLM to suggest new column mappings, with output constraints and pgvector for consistency.
posts.issue: Operations staff had to manually match many different supplier data schemas to a single internal format.

posts.title: From Activity to Intent: Generating User Journeys with LLMs
posts.summary: They fine‑tuned a 4 billion‑parameter LLM to read a user's activity timeline and output ranked journey names, distilling knowledge from a larger model and deploying it at notification scale.
posts.issue: Pinterest needed to identify users' long‑term goals, not just the last pin they clicked.

posts.title: Building Reliable Data Analytics Agents: Lessons from the KDD Cup
posts.summary: They built a small, clear harness that limited tools, unified all data into a single SQL view, added persistent Python state, and made every step inspectable.
posts.issue: Answering questions across many data sources caused agents to fail due to complex tool usage.

posts.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
posts.summary: They built Agent Lightning v1.0, a lightweight RL framework that inserts an LLM proxy between the agent and the model, letting the same harness used in production train directly.
posts.issue: Training agents with real-world tools was costly and mismatched the deployed version.

posts.title: Validate AI Factory Changes with Digital Twins and AI Agents
posts.summary: They created a digital‑twin simulation of the AI factory and AI agents that query the twin, run checks, and trigger workflows, letting CI/CD validate changes early.
posts.issue: Teams had to wait for physical hardware before they could test infrastructure and software changes, slowing deployments.

posts.title: Unlocking Earth AI’s planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health
posts.summary: Created a planetary geospatial foundation model that turns satellite, mobility, and search signals into monthly location embeddings, which can be dropped into existing health models without extra training.
posts.result: Embeddings matched or improved conventional inputs across many disease tasks
posts.issue: Public health data is slow, sparse, and split by borders, slowing response to outbreaks.

posts.title: Metrics Board: Building an Agent-ready Metrics Layer
posts.summary: They created Metrics Board, a platform that automates metric creation, enforces quality, and lets LLM agents query metrics in natural language.
posts.issue: Teams struggled with chaotic, unreliable metrics across a massive data lake, making decisions and experiments hard.

posts.title: Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development
posts.summary: Created a new storage layer and core services that scale to agent‑level traffic, using sharding, caching, and async pipelines to keep repository actions fast.
posts.issue: Developers needed Git operations that could handle thousands of AI agents working on code simultaneously.

posts.title: AI Agents Need Memory: Building Persistent Memory for Agentforce
posts.summary: Created a persistent memory layer that stores conversation context and task state, letting agents recall prior steps across sessions.
posts.issue: AI agents forgot previous interactions, making complex tasks hard to automate.

posts.title: Powering AI-led research through simulation
posts.summary: Created a fast, offline simulator called sim‑rs that runs a full city‑day of orders in minutes, letting agents experiment and evaluate strategies quickly.
posts.result: City‑day simulation completed in tens of minutes
posts.issue: Testing new dispatch strategies took weeks, limiting how many ideas could be tried.

posts.title: The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed.
posts.summary: They built ThinkingBox, a benchmark that runs agents, checks the final database state and side effects, and scores consistency across many runs.
posts.issue: AI agents seemed to work but often left incorrect data in the database.

posts.title: AutoSynthData: Generating Training Data for Enterprise Agents
posts.summary: They created AutoSynthData, a system that turns agent failures and a stronger teacher model's successes into many realistic tasks, validates them, and builds a curriculum that focuses on remaining weak spots.
posts.issue: Enterprises lacked enough training data for agents to handle their specific tools, rules, and data.

posts.title: Introducing AgentHub: Booking.com Platform for Modular Travel AI Agents
posts.summary: They built AgentHub, a configuration‑driven platform that lets teams assemble reusable LLM agents, connect them to internal APIs, and run multi‑step workflows.
posts.issue: Travel teams needed a fast way to create AI agents that could handle many booking tasks.

posts.title: Graph-centric agentic intelligence
posts.summary: Created an agent that walks real‑time dependency graphs, runs cascaded analytics, and uses causal inference to locate root causes automatically.
posts.result: 95% fault localization accuracy in under 30 seconds
posts.issue: Ops teams needed AI agents that could understand complex network graphs to pinpoint failures fast.

posts.title: Why I tried to kill token billing (and why we kept it)
posts.summary: Built a token‑billing system that records model usage, applies markups, and lets teams monitor costs, while keeping pricing logic separate from the invoice
posts.issue: Customers needed a way to track AI usage costs without exposing token details in invoices

posts.title: ShopGym: Realistic, reproducible sandboxes for shopping agents
posts.summary: They built ShopGym, a sandbox that copies live stores into resettable simulations and creates realistic shopping tasks, letting agents be evaluated consistently.
posts.issue: Developers struggled to train and test shopping agents because real stores constantly change and bots get blocked.

posts.title: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Nemotron for Saudi Arabic Dialects, with a Path to Other Languages
posts.summary: They curated a small dialect corpus, mixed it with existing data, and fine‑tuned Nemotron 3.5 using NVIDIA NeMo’s efficient batching recipe.
posts.issue: ASR struggled with Saudi Arabic dialects and local recording conditions.

posts.title: Build Local AI Apps with C++ and NVIDIA TensorRT RTX Samples
posts.summary: Created open‑source C++ samples that export models to ONNX, then use ONNX Runtime with TensorRT for fast GPU‑accelerated inference across platforms.
posts.issue: Developers needed a way to run AI models locally on Windows, Linux, and ARM without custom runtimes.

posts.title: Build Applications on NVIDIA BlueField Faster with NVIDIA DOCA Agent Skills
posts.summary: Created DOCA Agent Skills that give agents verified API signatures, hardware requirements, and build constraints, letting them reason like expert DOCA developers.
posts.issue: General AI agents lacked specific knowledge of NVIDIA DOCA, causing guesswork and slow development cycles.

posts.title: How Deterministic Controls Turn AI Output Into Reliable Prompt Templates
posts.summary: Implemented deterministic controls that turn free-form instructions into stable, safe prompt templates for the Prompt Builder.
posts.issue: Open-ended AI instructions produced inconsistent and unsafe outputs, making prompt templates unreliable.

posts.title: Tracing Agent Harness Behavior with NVIDIA NeMo Relay
posts.summary: They created NeMo Relay, which records every model and tool call, timing, and errors, letting developers trace and compare agent runs to find inefficiencies.
posts.issue: Developers can’t see why an agent takes extra steps or fails, making it hard to improve efficiency.

posts.title: Deploying an HSTU Generative Recommender with NVIDIA Dynamo-Triton
posts.summary: They built a generative recommender served with Dynamo‑Triton, using ahead‑of‑time compiled PyTorch, GPU‑backed KV caching, and an embedding cache to cut latency.
posts.issue: Personalized recommendations were slow because models had to process long user histories and large item tables.

posts.title: Introducing AI Ecosystem: Zoom Out to See Your Whole AI Agent Fleet
posts.summary: They built AI Ecosystem, a view that shows all agents, their calls, costs, and failures in one place, letting users drill into any conversation for details.
posts.issue: Teams running many agents found it hard to see what was wrong across the whole fleet.

posts.title: Agents Need Context: Introducing Canvas Connectors, Fleet-wide AI Agent Visibility, and More
posts.summary: Built Canvas, a live workspace that pulls in external data via connectors (GitHub, PagerDuty, Confluence, Jira) and shows evidence like graphs, enabling collaborative investigation of agent‑driven failures.
posts.issue: Teams run many AI agents and need more context to understand production incidents quickly.

posts.title: How Diffusion Controller unifies and simplifies AI image generation
posts.summary: They added a small controller network that continuously guides the diffusion steps, improving prompt alignment while keeping image quality, even on closed models.
posts.issue: Generated images often missed specific details or looked distorted when trying to follow exact prompts.

posts.title: Personalization without user identity
posts.summary: They created Proximity Features that group nearby anonymous users and use the group’s past behavior as signals, enabling instant, location‑based personalization without personal IDs.
posts.issue: New visitors arrive without login or history, so the system cannot personalize search and recommendations.

posts.title: Getting the Source Right, Not Just the Fact: Source-Aware Verification for MCP Agents
posts.summary: They created ProvenanceGuard, a verification step that checks each claim against the specific tool output it claims to come from, catching wrong attributions.
posts.issue: Agents mix information from many tools, making it hard to tell if answers cite the correct source.

posts.title: The making of the Yelp Assistant UI
posts.summary: Created a server‑driven UI where the backend sends layout and content, letting Yelp Assistant’s chat UI be updated instantly without new app releases.
posts.issue: Mobile app updates are slow, so UI changes take days to reach users.

posts.title: Evolving our calendar assistant Reclaim to be AI-native without starting over
posts.summary: They built an AI agent that reads free‑text requests, checks the calendar context, and creates appropriate scheduling actions while reusing the existing scheduler.
posts.issue: Users wanted to schedule tasks by describing goals in their own words, not by picking preset settings.

posts.title: Lower the Cost of Building and Running Visual AI Agents with NVIDIA VSS Blueprint 3.3
posts.summary: They released VSS Blueprint 3.3, adding a Build Vision Agent skill for rapid deployment and Adaptive Efficient Video Sampling that cuts VLM token use and GPU load.
posts.issue: Building visual AI agents was expensive and hard to maintain, especially for video ingestion, processing, and search.

posts.title: AI Native by Design: Lessons Learned from Building NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect
posts.summary: Created an open‑source C++ library where AI agents generate candidate implementations, then isolate, test, benchmark, and review each change before shipping.
posts.issue: Model developers struggled to get high‑performance TensorRT inference without deep expertise.

posts.title: Holo4: powering generalist computer-use agents
posts.summary: Holo4 was trained with supervised and reinforcement learning on many tasks, letting it click, type, write code, and call tools, and it runs on any platform with one model.
posts.issue: Businesses needed a single AI agent that could work with screens, code, and APIs without switching models.

posts.title: Engineering Multi-Agent AI Teams That Build and Test Themselves
posts.summary: They built self‑modifying agents that can design, verify, test, and fix other agents, automating the whole development loop.
posts.issue: Creating and testing AI agents manually was slow and error‑prone.

posts.title: NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform: A Reference for Continuous In-Silicon Agent Monitoring
posts.summary: Created OpenShell, an open‑source runtime that runs agents in a sandbox with kernel‑level isolation and continuous monitoring.
posts.issue: AI agents were breaking out of their test environments and accessing unauthorized systems.

posts.title: Add Runtime Controls to AI Agents with NVIDIA OpenShell
posts.summary: They created OpenShell, a sandbox that enforces policies, limits file and network access, and protects credentials for any AI agent without changing its code.
posts.issue: Agents could access too many resources, risking data leaks or unintended actions.

posts.title: A kernel-centric path to real-time video generation on Trainium
posts.summary: They engineered a kernel‑centric pipeline on AWS Trainium, optimizing inference scheduling, bin‑packing, and global networking to serve video frames quickly.
posts.issue: Users needed real‑time video generation with low latency and high efficiency at scale.

posts.title: Automating coherent long-form video generation
posts.summary: They built a multi‑agent system that plans and tracks visual continuity, coordinating diffusion models and other tools to keep scenes and characters consistent.
posts.result: Substantial gains in multi‑shot narrative consistency and character persistence
posts.issue: Long‑form video creation kept losing character look and story flow because separate tools failed and drifted.

posts.title: Agentic Platform: Open-Sourcing the Agentic Identity Broker
posts.summary: Created an open‑source identity broker that records delegation chains and securely exchanges tokens so agents can access third‑party systems on behalf of users.
posts.issue: Agents needed to act for users across services without storing users' access tokens.

posts.title: Agent Memory with Engram: A Practical Guide
posts.summary: Created Engram, a managed memory service that stores conversation data, extracts facts into topics, and lets agents search past memories before generating replies.
posts.issue: Agents struggled to keep track of past conversations, leading to repetitive or irrelevant responses.

posts.title: How Agoda is evolving engineering support with AI agents
posts.summary: Created OpsBot AI, an LLM‑powered Slack bot that reads engineers' problem descriptions, extracts relevant context, fills request forms, and routes tickets to the right team.
posts.issue: Engineers struggled to collect needed details and route support requests when issues were described in free text.

posts.title: AI Agent Observability: Making Silent Production Failures Visible and Actionable
posts.summary: The team created Agentforce Health Monitoring, which tracks agent uptime, logs metrics, and alerts ops teams to investigate issues quickly.
posts.issue: Silent failures of AI agents in production went unnoticed, hurting reliability.

posts.title: Helix: The internal tool powering our Shopify app's native migration
posts.summary: Created Helix, a tool that splits migration into tiny checkpoints with strict review gates, letting LLMs generate code step‑by‑step while engineers guide it.
posts.result: App rebuilt and published in 12 weeks
posts.issue: Migrating a large React Native app to native Swift/Kotlin was slow and error‑prone.

posts.title: The future of practice: Enabling teachers to create learning interactives with generative UI
posts.summary: They built a generative UI that lets teachers design guided, interactive simulations on demand, using learning‑design guardrails to keep content accurate and aligned with curriculum.
posts.issue: Teachers struggled to create engaging, interactive simulations for every lesson.

posts.title: Beyond Two Towers: Launching the 3-Tower Engagement Co-Train Model (Part 2)
posts.summary: Created a 3‑tower co‑train model that shares embeddings, gives a fast two‑tower score for all ads and a richer three‑tower score for a selected subset, keeping latency low.
posts.issue: Ads needed more accurate click predictions without slowing down serving millions of candidates.

posts.title: The guest journey, updated in real time: extending Airbnb’s sequence recommender with Chronon
posts.summary: Added near‑real‑time model transforms and push mode to Chronon, instantly updating guest embeddings as they browse, so the ranking model sees fresh data.
posts.issue: Guest activity from the same day wasn’t reflected in rankings, making recommendations stale.

posts.title: ML based ranking using Nrtsearch
posts.summary: They added an Inference Plugin to Nrtsearch that runs ML models like XGBoost inside the search engine, extracting features from documents and re‑ranking results on‑the‑fly.
posts.issue: Search relevance suffered because traditional term‑based scoring couldn't use rich signals or learn feature weights.

posts.title: How Data 360 Builds Trusted Context: The Enduring Layer for Enterprise AI
posts.summary: Created Data 360 Trusted Context, a layer that selects the smallest needed data slice, checks permissions, and retrieves it on‑demand for LLM calls.
posts.issue: Need relevant, authorized enterprise data for each AI request without sending all data in the prompt.

posts.title: Designing Claude for ears, not eyes: An accessibility skill for blind and low-vision users
posts.summary: They added rules to the model’s instructions so it speaks clearly and follows screen‑reader conventions, making the assistant usable by audio‑only users
posts.issue: Blind and low‑vision users struggled to use the chatbot because it was designed for visual interaction

posts.title: Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement
posts.summary: Built an investigation framework that extracts, embeds, and clusters data, automating the methodology so teams can run analyses at scale without manual curation.
posts.issue: Need a repeatable, auditable way to analyze large support chats for AI product safety.

posts.title: Your Agent Aced the Task. Will It Do It Again?
posts.summary: They added a Consistency Analyzer and new consistency guidelines to their ALTK‑Evolve system, which turn past agent runs into rules that are applied at inference to keep the agent on the same path each time.
posts.issue: Agents sometimes give different answers to the same request, causing unreliable behavior.

posts.title: How Canvas Powers the AI Agent Development Feedback Loop
posts.summary: Built Canvas to bring telemetry, code history, tickets, and chat into one workspace, letting teams investigate, prioritize, and validate changes automatically.
posts.issue: Users struggled to track agent performance and fix issues across scattered tools.

posts.title: How AI Agents Get Trusted Customer Context with Data 360 Data Graphs
posts.summary: They built a Data 360 graph that stores verified customer data and connects it to Agentforce, letting agents retrieve trusted context in real time.
posts.issue: Agents lacked reliable, up‑to‑date customer information, leading to generic or incorrect responses.

posts.title: Evolving Pinterest’s Embedding Retrieval Platform
posts.summary: They upgraded their internal search platform to use quantized integer vectors, hybrid queries and more flexible indexing, cutting memory use while keeping latency low.
posts.issue: Embedding search was becoming too expensive and slow as the number of items grew into tens of billions.

posts.title: Migrating Shop app from React Native to native
posts.summary: The team used AI coding agents to translate React Native screens into native SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, rebuilding the Shop app in 12 weeks.
posts.issue: Maintaining a shared React Native codebase limited performance and added complexity for iOS and Android.

posts.title: Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify
posts.summary: Shopify used advanced LLM agents to generate native Swift and Kotlin code, making native development as fast and cheap as using React Native.
posts.issue: Building mobile apps in both Swift and Kotlin doubled development effort and cost.

posts.title: Building Pinterest’s VLM Serving Stack on NVIDIA Dynamo
posts.summary: Pinterest built a VLM serving stack on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and Dynamo, using distributed inference, KV cache offloading, and custom routing to handle image‑heavy requests efficiently.
posts.issue: Serving vision‑language models needed low‑latency, cost‑effective inference for Pinterest’s multimodal features.

posts.title: HFresh: Memory-Efficient Vector Search
posts.summary: They built HFresh, a disk‑based index that partitions vectors into small on‑disk postings and uses an in‑memory centroid index to limit disk reads, keeping memory low while maintaining high recall.
posts.issue: Users needed fast vector search but had limited memory and large datasets.

posts.title: Enterprise AI Accuracy: Building a More Trustworthy RAG Application
posts.summary: They added validation steps, stricter retrieval filters, and post‑generation checks to ensure retrieved data matches the query and is formatted correctly before answering.
posts.issue: The RAG system often returned incorrect or garbled information, confusing users and risking trust.

posts.title: Wide Events vs. Three Pillars: AI Observability Costs
posts.summary: They switched to wide events—a single data format that captures metrics, logs, and traces together—so all telemetry fits in one storage layer and reduces overhead.
posts.issue: AI agents were driving up observability costs because metrics, logs, and traces were stored separately.

posts.title: Agentic Machine Learning Modeling at Instacart
posts.summary: They built AI agents that suggest, code, and evaluate model options, letting engineers focus on oversight.
posts.issue: ML engineers spent too much time manually choosing models and settings.

posts.title: Fine-tuning a 350M Model for Better Structured Outputs in 100 GRPO Steps
posts.summary: Fine‑tuned a 350M LLM with Group Relative Policy Optimization using the TRL library, running only 100 steps on a free‑tier GPU, raising structured‑output accuracy on IFStruct.
posts.issue: Models often output data in the wrong format, preventing integration into downstream systems.

posts.title: Give Your Coding Agents a Memory You Own
posts.summary: Created a local memory layer called funes that indexes agent session logs, chunks them, embeds them, and reranks results so agents can retrieve exact past turns during new tasks.
posts.issue: Coding agents forget previous work when a session ends, forcing users to re‑enter context.

posts.title: Portal by Spotify cut my Claude Code token usage by 90%
posts.summary: They created two lightweight agent modes that handle I/O with a cheaper model, reserving the expensive model for complex reasoning.
posts.issue: Users spent too many tokens on simple file reading tasks.

posts.title: How River takes security work from a fix to merge
posts.summary: They built River, an AI agent in Slack that automates checking, updating, and merging patches, and routes decisions to engineers when needed.
posts.result: Backlog down 70%, merge rate rose to 80%
posts.issue: Security teams struggled with slow, manual patch handling and a growing backlog of vulnerability fixes.

posts.title: How we make AI coding more cost efficient without sacrificing task quality
posts.summary: They added caching, switched to smaller distilled models, and batched requests, cutting compute while keeping answer quality unchanged.
posts.issue: AI coding features were expensive to run, raising costs for users and limiting scalability.

posts.title: How to extract meaning from charts and tables in PDFs
posts.summary: They built a RAG system that embeds whole PDF pages as images, letting a late‑interaction model see charts and tables directly without extra OCR or chunking steps.
posts.issue: Users couldn’t find data hidden in charts or tables inside PDFs, so answers were wrong or missing.

posts.title: Mapping global methane emissions from space with deep learning
posts.summary: They built MAPL‑EMIT, a deep‑learning model that turns hyperspectral satellite images into detections, enhancements, and source estimates of methane plumes.
posts.issue: Users needed a fast way to spot methane leaks from space.

posts.title: TimesFM-3: A zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
posts.summary: They built TimesFM‑3, a 330‑million‑parameter transformer pre‑trained on over 1 trillion time points, that can forecast multiple series together in one pass without fine‑tuning.
posts.issue: Users needed accurate forecasts that consider many related signals, but existing models only used single series data.

posts.title: Planetary prediction engine: Automating global models via Earth AI
posts.summary: They built an autonomous system that, from a natural‑language query, automatically finds relevant geospatial data, engineers features, trains and evaluates a model, and produces a report.
posts.issue: Manual data curation for geospatial models took weeks, slowing critical responses.
posts.result: Reduced model build time from weeks to minutes

posts.title: When LLM judges agree, should we believe them?
posts.summary: They built a system that checks how judges agree independently, then weights their votes based on that independence, improving accuracy by 9–14%.
posts.issue: Users needed a reliable way to judge if retrieved text was useful, but many LLM judges made similar mistakes.

posts.title: GlucoFM: Foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring
posts.summary: They trained a lightweight self‑supervised model that splits glucose signals into slow trends and quick spikes, learning useful features from many unlabeled readings.
posts.issue: Users lacked accurate ways to predict diabetes risk from cheap glucose data.
posts.result: PR‑AUC improved 5.8 percentage points over the best prior model

posts.title: Training and Finetuning Multi-Vector Embedding Models with Sentence Transformers
posts.summary: Finetuned a multi‑vector encoder using Sentence Transformers, training it on domain data with custom loss and evaluation, achieving stronger token‑level matching.
posts.issue: Search quality on medical texts was poor with generic models.

posts.title: The Context Tax of Agentic Development
posts.summary: They added explicit, structured context that maps UI URLs to actual backends, so both humans and agents can verify and act on the correct environment.
posts.issue: Engineers and agents struggled because environment URLs hid the real backend, causing wrong work and delays.

posts.title: Granite 4.2 LLMs: How They're Built
posts.summary: We built Granite 4.2 by pre‑training a dense decoder, fine‑tuning on chain‑of‑thought data, then applying multi‑stage reinforcement learning that teaches tool use and reasoning, releasing 3 B, 8 B, and 30 B versions.
posts.issue: We needed a language model that could reason step‑by‑step and use external tools when needed.

posts.title: SOP-Bench: A new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real business procedures
posts.summary: Amazon created SOP‑Bench, a benchmark with real SOPs, tools, and true answers, so agents are scored on actually completing tasks, not just generating text.
posts.issue: AI agents struggled to follow real business procedures that need background knowledge and judgment.

posts.title: Does it matter how you feed an agent its context?
posts.summary: They compared four ways to give the agent context—single prompt, handoff notes, etc.—and measured cost and performance for the same coding job.
posts.issue: Engineers ran out of token budget while using a coding agent for a complex backend task.

posts.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data
posts.summary: They built a multi‑agent system that iteratively generates hypotheses, runs statistical tests, trains models, and checks literature to rank biomarkers, all under human supervision.
posts.issue: Users needed trustworthy biomarkers from wearable data, but existing tools missed statistical rigor.
posts.result: Recovered known signals, found new convergent biomarkers, and boosted prediction accuracy

posts.title: How Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, Jobs, and Buckets Power Search on Papers with Code
posts.summary: Created a hybrid search system that mixes fast keyword lookup with semantic vector embeddings, combines results with reciprocal rank fusion, and uses rerankers for better relevance.
posts.issue: Researchers struggled to find relevant papers quickly, especially with vague queries, typos, or missing keywords.

posts.title: Building Jarvis Pro: Route first, answer later
posts.summary: Created Jarvis Pro that first classifies each user request, then loads only the needed data and generates an answer, using a routing guide to enforce safe paths.
posts.result: Safe routing 99.4% accuracy, quality score rose to 91.0
posts.issue: Account managers needed reliable AI advice for merchant meetings without giving wrong recommendations.

posts.title: Up to 3.2x Faster Inference with LFM2.5-DSpark
posts.summary: They added a lightweight draft model that predicts tokens first, then the main model verifies them, cutting memory reads and speeding up decoding.
posts.issue: LLM inference was slow, causing high latency for users.

posts.title: Building Menu Vision: Real-Time Dish Recognition
posts.summary: Created an on‑device camera app that reads menu text, matches it to Yelp’s dish database, and instantly shows user photos using real‑time vision and fuzzy matching.
posts.issue: Diners had to type each menu item to see photos, slowing decisions at the table.

posts.title: Gisting: Compressing LLM Agent context to ↑ throughput and ↓ cost
posts.summary: They replaced thousands of prompt tokens with a few learned “gist” tokens, training the embeddings by distilling from the full prompt so the model behaves the same.
posts.result: Latency dropped from 6.8s to 4.2s, throughput rose from 20.2 to 23.4 QPS
posts.issue: Long prompts made the agent slow and expensive to run.

posts.title: How we knew COVID was over (and what our models had to unlearn)
posts.summary: They created a process to decide whether to refit, redesign, or keep a model unchanged, analyzing bias before updating forecasts.
posts.issue: Forecasts kept missing actual demand after COVID, causing biased planning decisions.

posts.title: Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Embedding Models with Sentence Transformers
posts.summary: They added a multi‑vector model that stores a vector for each token, matching queries token‑by‑token with a MaxSim operation, improving retrieval quality.
posts.issue: Single-vector embeddings lose detail, hurting search accuracy for specific queries.

posts.title: How Much Memory Does Your Agent Actually Need?
posts.summary: They built a system that distills past actions into guidelines, then injects either the full set or a compact, task‑specific subset at inference, tuning the amount per model size.
posts.issue: Agents needed to know how much past‑task memory to keep without hurting cost or performance.

posts.title: Faire’s agentic development culture
posts.summary: They built lightweight layers around existing models, encouraging voluntary use and showing benefits to drive natural adoption.
posts.issue: Engineers wanted to use advanced AI tools early without waiting for vendors.

posts.title: Black-box pen tests on Replit
posts.summary: They added black‑box penetration tests that run in a sandbox, simulating an attacker’s browser actions while also running a white‑box scan on the code.
posts.issue: Builders needed fast, affordable security checks for their apps before launch.

posts.title: Building Foundry Part 2: Where creative workflows break
posts.summary: They built Foundry on Weaviate, using semantic embeddings and vector search to keep files findable despite chaotic folder and tagging practices.
posts.issue: Retrieval stopped working as projects grew and metadata quality slipped.

posts.title: Record, train, and deploy from one place with Strands Agents, LeRobot, and Hugging Face Storage Buckets
posts.summary: Created a continuous loop where robot demos are stored in Hugging Face Storage Buckets, read directly for training, and deployed back, avoiding redundant transfers.
posts.issue: Repeated data uploads and downloads slowed training and increased costs as robot recordings grew.

posts.title: Agentic Engineering at Zalando: a snapshot
posts.summary: Created a LiteLLM API proxy with pre/post hooks for cost tracking, model retirement, and prompt‑caching injection, plus a chat UI and CLI, running on tiny pods.
posts.result: Supports 2k MAU with six small pods
posts.issue: Engineers struggled to experiment with LLMs across providers and track usage costs.

posts.title: Introducing OlmoEarth embeddings: Custom embedding exports from OlmoEarth Studio for downstream analysis
posts.summary: OlmoEarth Studio now lets users run a model on chosen images and download the resulting embedding vectors as lightweight GeoTIFF files, with options for resolution, time range, and fine‑tuning.
posts.issue: Users needed a simple, cheap way to turn satellite images into numeric vectors for search and analysis.

posts.title: Grab Bench: Evaluating AI on Grab-shaped production work
posts.summary: They created Grab Bench, a configurable evaluation harness that runs AI models through task plugins, records results, and uses deterministic scorers or LLM judges to spot failures.
posts.issue: Engineers couldn't trust AI outputs because subtle, plausible errors slipped past checks.

posts.title: Scaling Test-Time Compute in Search Mode
posts.summary: Added an effort setting that lets the query agent spend more time breaking down queries and reranking results, with three tiers from medium to ultrahigh.
posts.issue: Complex queries needed better search accuracy, but users also cared about speed and cost.

posts.title: How Keras 3 Helped Modernise Expedia Group’s Lodging Ranking Stack
posts.summary: They rewrote the training and serving pipelines with Keras 3, modern GPU optimisations, and cleaner APIs, making training 30% faster and cutting P99 inference latency by two‑thirds.
posts.issue: Slow training and high latency slowed new ranking model releases.

posts.title: How we selected the next vector database at Booking.com
posts.summary: They built a shared vector‑search infrastructure, evaluated different databases, and chose a new system that supports hybrid search, large capacity, and high request rates.
posts.issue: Teams needed a fast, scalable vector store that could handle many use cases and high traffic.

posts.title: Build Low-Latency Multilingual Voice Agents: Open Weights & Full Deployment Control with NVIDIA Magpie TTS
posts.summary: They built a modular speech pipeline using NVIDIA Magpie TTS with open weights, letting them run ASR, LLM, and TTS on their own hardware and tune each part for speed.
posts.issue: Voice responses were too slow, making the whole conversation feel laggy for users.

posts.title: CI Doesn’t Need On-Demand: Moving Our Build Pipelines to Spot Instances
posts.summary: Created a self‑healing Kubernetes layer for GitHub Actions that runs most jobs on spot instances, detects terminations, retries jobs and cleans up pods automatically.
posts.issue: CI pipelines were too expensive or unreliable when using cheap spot instances.

posts.title: Spec, review, ship: How AI is changing the way Faire builds software
posts.summary: They built a shared specification workflow and AI agents that generate, review, and orchestrate code tasks, letting engineers focus on judgment.
posts.issue: Engineers struggled to turn vague ideas into working code quickly across many tech stacks.

posts.title: LLMs for Relevance: Automating High-Quality Product Relevance Labeling in Flipkart Search
posts.summary: They trained an LLM to judge query‑product relevance, first with supervised fine‑tuning and then with Grouped Relative Policy Optimization to improve consistency.
posts.issue: Manual relevance labeling was slow, expensive, and noisy.
posts.result: Matches or beats human annotators at a fraction of the cost

posts.title: How AI is transforming analytics at Grab
posts.summary: Created an AI agent that automates data prep, query writing, analysis, and report drafting, letting users get answers in minutes.
posts.issue: Analysts spent weeks preparing data and generating insights, slowing business decisions.

posts.title: Kafka App? There’s a Skill for That
posts.summary: Implemented a Kafka streaming pipeline that continuously updates feature vectors and embeddings, feeding them into the recommendation engine in near real‑time.
posts.issue: Shoppers needed up‑to‑date recommendations, but data lagged behind their browsing activity.

posts.title: Focus on the Feature, Not the Fixture: GenAI powered GraphQL mocks
posts.summary: They created mockql‑rs, a CLI that reads a GraphQL query with @mock tags, checks the schema, and asks an LLM to fill in only the annotated fields, producing schema‑valid mock responses on the fly.
posts.issue: Developers spent hours creating and updating hand‑written GraphQL mock data that quickly became outdated.

posts.title: Crowdsourced taxonomy verification: A feedback-driven framework for refining knowledge graph relationships via online search interactions
posts.summary: They created a loop that shows unverified graph links in search suggestions, watches user clicks, and uses that feedback to confirm or reject the links, continuously refining the graph.
posts.issue: Wrong relationships in the knowledge graph gave users irrelevant search results and low trust.

posts.title: Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model
posts.summary: They built a multi‑agent harness that scans code, runs tests, and automatically opens pull requests with fixes.
posts.issue: Security teams needed a fast, reliable way to find and fix code vulnerabilities.

posts.title: Virtual Packer: How Faire estimates shipping costs at checkout
posts.summary: They built a Virtual Packer that predicts package weight and count, then queries live carrier rates to show a real‑time estimate.
posts.issue: Boutique owners need accurate shipping cost at checkout, but actual rates are unknown until after shipping.

posts.title: Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale
posts.summary: They built an eval‑driven development framework that uses AI judges, synthetic tests, and human review to continuously catch and fix errors.
posts.issue: Airbnb needed a reliable way to test and improve unpredictable LLM features.

posts.title: NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams: Bringing Real-Time Generative Simulation to Surgical Robotics
posts.summary: Created a real‑time generative simulator that predicts video outcomes from robot motions, using a distilled student model running on one RTX GPU.
posts.issue: Testing surgical robot actions is slow, costly, and risky on real hardware.

posts.title: Bringing Nunchaku 4-bit Diffusion Inference to Diffusers
posts.summary: Integrated 4-bit weight and activation quantization (SVDQuant) into Diffusers, letting users load Nunchaku checkpoints without custom code, cutting memory and speeding inference.
posts.issue: Large diffusion models need too much GPU memory and run slowly on consumer GPUs.

posts.title: Autoscience: How we built agent-driven ML exploration at Faire
posts.summary: Built Autoscience, an agent system that proposes, runs, and evaluates model experiments with persistent memory and steering hooks, enabling many more iterations.
posts.result: Production model accuracy improved double‑digit percentages
posts.issue: ML teams could only try a tiny fraction of possible model changes, limiting performance.

posts.title: How our universal content processing platform Riviera evolved for AI and beyond
posts.summary: Built Riviera, a shared platform that converts files into thumbnails, PDFs, and lightweight videos, scaling to handle billions of transformations daily.
posts.issue: Users needed fast, consistent previews and AI-ready content across many file types.

posts.title: The Self-Driving Company
posts.summary: Replit built a network of AI agents that take goals, gather context, perform work, verify results, and hand off to humans when needed, automating tasks across the company.
posts.issue: Teams needed help with repetitive tasks like incident triage and code reviews, slowing progress.

posts.title: Running Hermes at Razorpay: a Network-isolated, Self-improving “Second Brain” for every Employee
posts.summary: Created an isolated Kubernetes platform that gives each employee a dedicated Hermes agent, sandboxed storage, and scheduled jobs, letting the agent learn and act autonomously.
posts.issue: Employees needed personal AI assistants that could run continuously without risking security or data leaks.

posts.title: From Traditional ML to AI Agents: How Booking.com Scales AI Observability With Arize AI
posts.summary: They integrated Arize AI to collect telemetry and trace every prompt, model call, retrieval and tool use, giving end‑to‑end visibility for all AI systems.
posts.issue: Complex AI workflows were hard to debug because many steps happen behind the scenes.

posts.title: Capturing token IDs during agentic interactions for better reinforcement learning
posts.summary: Created Turnstile, a Rust proxy that sits between the agent harness and the model, capturing every token ID as it’s generated and exporting a clean trajectory for RL trainers.
posts.issue: RL training needed exact token‑level logs of agent actions, but transcripts lost crucial details.

posts.title: Multi-Agent Collaboration on a Shared Canvas
posts.summary: They created Honeycomb Canvas, a shared whiteboard where each engineer has an independent AI agent that can run in its own isolated micro‑VM yet see peers' work, enabling coordinated, parallel debugging.
posts.issue: Engineers needed to debug production issues together without their AI assistants interfering with each other's investigations.

posts.title: Consistent Generative Video: Building Video Models That Remember
posts.summary: They trained tiny LoRA adapters on two video diffusion models, keeping the base frozen and adding only ~0.1% new parameters per layer, enabling fast, scalable character‑specific generation.
posts.issue: Users wanted realistic talking‑head videos of IP characters without reshooting, but existing models drifted in identity and lip sync.

posts.title: Introducing TabFM: A zero-shot foundation model for tabular data
posts.summary: They built TabFM, a foundation model that uses in‑context learning to predict on any tabular data in one forward pass, removing the need for training or feature engineering.
posts.issue: Data scientists spent too much time training and tuning models for each new table.

posts.title: Using LLMs to Analyze Spark SQL Plans: A Practical Approach to Debugging Long-Running Jobs
posts.summary: They built an LLM‑driven tool that reads structured Spark SQL plans, matches them against defined anti‑patterns, and returns JSON‑formatted fixes tied to specific plan nodes.
posts.issue: Engineers spent hours debugging slow Spark jobs without clear clues, leading to over‑provisioned clusters and higher costs.

posts.title: Instrumenting AI Agents for the Agent Timeline: A Practical OpenTelemetry Guide
posts.summary: They added OpenTelemetry spans with a shared conversation ID to every model, tool, and downstream call, letting Honeycomb render a full timeline of the agent’s actions.
posts.issue: Debugging multi-step AI agents in production was hard because failures showed only vague model errors.

posts.title: Accelerating Gemini Nano models on Pixel with frozen Multi-Token Prediction
posts.summary: They added Multi-Token Prediction to frozen Gemini Nano models, letting the phone generate several words at once and cut energy use.
posts.issue: On-device LLMs were too slow and drained battery, hurting user experience.

posts.title: How we used DSPy to turn AI evaluations into better responses in Dash chat
posts.summary: They built a layered evaluation system using LLM judges, calibrated it with human labels, then used DSPy to tune the agent’s prompts, creating a feedback loop that improved answer completeness and cut token use.
posts.result: Fewer incomplete answers and reduced token usage
posts.issue: Chat agent often gave incomplete answers and used many tokens, hurting user experience.

posts.title: Clustering billions of products for agentic commerce with Catalog API
posts.summary: They built an LLM‑driven pipeline that creates embeddings for each product, clusters them with a precision‑first threshold, and assigns a universal product ID so AI shopping agents can search a unified catalog.
posts.issue: Shopify needed to match the same real‑world products across billions of merchant listings that use different structures.

posts.title: From pixels to planning: Earth AI for nature restoration
posts.summary: They trained a high‑resolution deep‑learning model on satellite imagery to detect and convert tiny ecological features into precise vector shapes that can be used for planning and carbon accounting.
posts.issue: Users couldn’t see small hedgerows and woodlands on satellite maps, making it hard to plan nature restoration.

posts.title: Teaching Sidekick to say no: automated data curation with LLM judge consensus
posts.summary: Created an automated pipeline where several LLMs vote on whether a query should be refused, generated refusal examples, and fine‑tuned the model with this data.
posts.issue: The assistant never learned to refuse impossible merchant requests, leading to bad answers.

posts.title: How Dropbox uses MCP and Dash to close the design-to-code security gap
posts.summary: They built a system that uses a model‑context protocol, large language models, and Dropbox's Dash search to automatically pull relevant threat models into code reviews and check code against those requirements.
posts.issue: Security requirements often get lost between design review and code review, making it hard to verify compliance.

posts.title: How to make the case for giving your AI Agent system access
posts.summary: They added system access to the AI Agent, turning simple scripted tasks into full‑process procedures that can read and write data in CRM, billing, and order tools.
posts.issue: Customers asked for changes that the AI could explain but not execute, so support reps still had to intervene.

posts.title: Agentic Testing: Where Agents Fit in the E2E Testing Stack
posts.summary: They built LLM‑powered agents that automatically generate and run exploratory E2E tests, then compare results with deterministic test suites.
posts.issue: Testing teams struggled to cover all user paths in end‑to‑end tests.

posts.title: Extending Fin as the most open Agent platform
posts.summary: They created an open Agent platform with public APIs, CLI, and a proprietary model, letting HubSpot and Freshdesk users add the agent in under an hour.
posts.issue: Customers wanted an AI agent that could work inside their existing helpdesk without switching vendors.

posts.title: Taming a Million Tickets: How a Small Team Used AI to Modernize an Overgrown Jira Instance at Scale
posts.summary: They built an LLM‑powered system that read ticket data, identified patterns, and automatically migrated tickets to a unified configuration.
posts.issue: Over a million Jira tickets were scattered across 245 projects with inconsistent fields and workflows.

posts.title: Unlocking dependable responses with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform’s Agentic RAG
posts.summary: Built a multi‑agent RAG system that plans, reasons, and iteratively searches across corpora, confirming enough context before answering.
posts.issue: Enterprise queries often need multiple data sources, causing incomplete answers from single-step retrieval.

posts.title: Build a custom Shopify storefront on Replit
posts.summary: Replit built an Agent that chats with users, provisions a Shopify store, generates a custom front‑end, and links everything, all from a single conversation.

posts.title: Meet Replit SEO Agent

posts.summary: They created a new metric, Native Time to Interactive (NTTI), to measure when key screen components load and become usable, turning performance into a first‑class signal.
posts.issue: Users felt login screens were slow, eroding trust without obvious errors.
